Deputy

The County Assessor has the duty to value all real and personal
property in the county as a basis for the county board to levy
taxes. The assessor must be certified by the Department of Property
Assessment and Taxation and attention continuing education to keep
this certification.
The County Assessor is an elected official who has the general
supervision over the direction of the assessment of all property in
his or her county. The duties are prescribed by Nebraska Statues,
Rules and Regulations (Chapter 77), which have the effect of law.
Hayes County Real Estate Property Search Available Online
Real Estate Property Search
The records of the Hayes County Assessor are now available
online. You can search for official records by Owner or Parcel ID or
Address or Legal Description.
The following is a partial list of those duties.
Administer the assessment statues of Nebraska law.
Establish and maintain fair and equitable value on all real
and personal property within the county.
Attend all meetings of the County Board of Equalization.
Review all applications for religious, charitable and
educational tax exemptions.
Maintain cadastral records (i.e., parcel maps) on all
property in the county.
Prepare abstract of value and certification of taxes levied
for State Property Tax Administrator.
Prepare annual tax roll for the County Treasurer.
Attend mandatory workshops.
Obtain a minimum of 4- hours of continued education
bi-yearly.
